items.title: Always Asking People to Ask
items.summary: Luke Wroblewski argues that chat AI UIs make a mistake by defaulting to an empty prompt box — users often don't know what to ask, so starting with a pre-filled suggestion or sample answer gets better results than waiting for the user to go first.
items.why: The blank-slate problem is exactly what Cuemath's AI tutoring UI faces the moment a student opens a session; this is direct, actionable design guidance on how to make that first moment less intimidating and more productive.

items.title: "AI-Powered" Isn't a Position
items.summary: A positioning playbook for AI products arguing that 'AI-powered' is a feature description, not a strategy — with a framework for building a genuinely differentiated brand when every competitor is making the same claim.
items.why: Directly useful as Cuemath figures out how to distinguish its AI tutoring from a crowded edtech field; the playbook's competitive positioning framework applies across both product and brand decisions Manik is navigating.

items.title: De Bijloke
items.summary: Type documentation for De Bijloke, a Ghent music venue with 13th-century roots, where Pentagram's Marina Willer built an identity around a custom typeface designed to hold together a richly varied cultural programme.
items.why: Institutional identity at the highest craft level — a single flexible type system serving a diverse, centuries-old venue is a useful reference for how CueDesign might hold together Cuemath's own multi-surface product ecosystem.

items.title: Manchester City Women becomes the first WSL team to have its own distinct identity
items.summary: Nomad Studio designed a standalone visual identity for Manchester City Women FC — a monogram built from 'light' — giving the women's team its own distinct presence separate from the parent club.
items.why: A clean case study in sub-brand differentiation within a parent brand system, with a clear design rationale — the strategy is directly relevant to how Cuemath thinks about its practice app, tutoring product, and brand coexisting as distinct surfaces.

items.title: How Form solved the classic two-logo lockup problem for British Cycling and Lloyds
items.summary: Studio Form designed British Cycling's identity by baking both brand marks — club and title sponsor — into a single typographic system from the start, so there was never a clashing-logos problem to negotiate after the fact.
items.why: The 'solve the constraint in the system' approach is directly applicable to design systems work — building co-brand or sponsor flexibility into the foundation rather than retrofitting it, which is a recurring challenge in any multi-stakeholder product.
